requirements.text: The system shall be platform independent and function properly on any operating system.
The system shall be designed in such a way as to minimize the number of windows opened by the application.
The system shall be developed using the Java programming language.
The system shall be completed by December 2001.

Any operation requiring the user to supply a file name shall allow the user either to select the files from a list derived from files in the currently open application or to key in a file name, a relative path name, or a complete path name.
For any operation where the user is prompted to select from a list, the user shall be able to cancel the operation.
The HATS-GUI shall overwrite any file whose name is generated automatically.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to specify the number of levels of nodes to expand during SDT viewing.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to select the colors for types of displayed nodes in a displayed graph.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to select the shapes for types of displayed nodes in a displayed graph.
The HATS-GUI shall be able to communicate with Sun Solaris, Linux, and Windows 2000.

The HATS-GUI shall allow a user to create an application minimally consisting of a lexical specification file, a grammar file, a user-defined functions file, and application configuration information.
All files associated with a given application shall be stored in one directory.
The system shall open a new window when the user selects to display output.
Display windows opened by the system shall have buttons for closing the windows.

The system shall verify that automatically generated files are restricted to the application's designated working directory and prompt for confirmation if an existing file is not owned by the current application context.
The system shall validate that all external processes are executed from a pre-defined, read-only whitelist of trusted binaries and sanitize all command-line arguments to prevent command injection.
The system shall limit the number of concurrent output display windows to a maximum of 5, reusing existing windows for subsequent outputs if the limit is reached.
The system shall limit the number of concurrent display windows to a maximum of 5, or implement a tabbed interface to manage memory and screen real estate.
The system shall maintain a UI response time of less than 200ms for all user interactions on all supported platforms (Sun Solaris, Linux, Windows 2000).

OPEN: The PRD mentions file operations (read/write/delete) but does not specify any authorization or permission checks for file access, which is critical for multi-user environments or shared systems. - The HATS-GUI shall enforce file system permissions and ensure that all file operations are restricted to the user's authorized directory scope.

OPEN: The requirement to overwrite files automatically without user confirmation poses a significant risk of data loss for generated artifacts. - The HATS-GUI shall provide a user-configurable setting to enable or disable automatic overwriting of generated files, with a default of 'prompt before overwrite'.

OPEN: The requirement to 'open a new window' for every output display conflicts with the requirement to 'minimize the number of windows'. - The system shall display output in a single, reusable workspace window, or provide a tabbed interface to manage multiple outputs without spawning excessive new windows.

OPEN: The PRD does not define the expected scale of the Syntax Derivation Trees (SDTs) or the number of files per application. - The system shall support the display and manipulation of SDTs containing up to 10,000 nodes and applications containing up to 500 files without exceeding 500ms latency for navigation operations.
